13. Privacy Notice — overview

This Privacy Notice explains what information we collect, how we use and share it, and the choices you have. It applies to all U.S. residents who use the Service.

14. Information we collect

  • Denial and appeal information you provide: the denial letter text or an uploaded photo/PDF (which we convert to text), your insurer and plan details, procedure and any code, your answers to the appeal questions, and anything you write in the optional “your story” field.
  • Policy documents you optionally upload, as described in Section 16.
  • Technical data needed to operate and secure the Service, such as request logs and general device/connection information.

Please do not submit information you do not wish to share, and avoid including other people’s information unless you are authorized to do so.

15. How we use information

  • To locate the insurer’s published coverage policy for your procedure and prepare your action plan and, when appropriate, a draft appeal letter.
  • To operate, secure, maintain, and improve the Service.
  • To comply with law and enforce these Terms.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not use it for third-party advertising.

16. Optional sharing of a de-identified policy copy

If you upload your plan’s coverage document, we ask separately—through a checkbox that is off by default—whether we may keep a de-identified copy of that policy document to help the next patient on the same plan. This is optional; the Service works the same if you decline. When you consent, we keep the policy document only—not your name, member ID, or denial letter—screen the copy for personal identifiers, verify it before it is ever shown to another user, and flag it as possibly out of date after about 90 days. You may ask us to remove a document you contributed at any time.

17. How we share information

We share information only with service providers that help us run the Service (for example, the AI and search providers used to research policies and draft letters) under contracts that limit their use of it; in connection with a business transfer; and when required by law or to protect rights and safety. We do not sell personal information.

18. Security

We use reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards designed to protect information, including encrypted transport and encryption of sensitive data at rest, access controls, and scheduled deletion of older data. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

19. Data retention

We keep information only as long as needed to provide the Service and for a limited period afterward, then delete or de-identify it, except where longer retention is required by law. You may request deletion as described below.

20. Your privacy rights

Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or receive a copy of your personal information, and to opt out of certain processing. We do not sell personal information or use it for “targeted advertising” or “profiling” with legal effects.

California residents (CCPA/CPRA) may request access, deletion, correction, and information about our data practices, and are entitled to non-discrimination for exercising these rights. Residents of other states with comprehensive privacy laws (including, for example, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, and others as they take effect) have comparable rights. To exercise any right, contact us at [CONTACT EMAIL]; we will verify your request and respond as required by applicable law.

21. Children

The Service is intended for adults handling their own or an authorized person’s insurance appeal and is not directed to children under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.
